pilot_atoms.title: Ammeter and voltmeter readings in a DC circuit with parallel branches

question.statement: An ideal ammeter (zero resistance) and an ideal voltmeter (infinite resistance) are connected as shown. The ammeter and voltmeter reading for $R_{1} = 5\,\Omega$, $R_{2} = 15\,\Omega$, $R_{3} = 1.25\,\Omega$ and $E = 20\text{ V}$ are given as

figure_refs.caption: Circuit diagram showing parallel branches with $R_1 = 5\,\Omega$ in series with an ammeter, and $R_2 = 15\,\Omega$, connected in series with $R_3 = 1.25\,\Omega$ and a parallel voltmeter across $R_3$, powered by an EMF source $E = 20\text{ V}$.
figure_refs.alt_text: Electrical circuit diagram with a DC voltage source of 20 V connected to a network. The network consists of a parallel combination of two branches: one branch containing resistor R1 = 5 ohms in series with an ideal ammeter A, and the second branch containing resistor R2 = 15 ohms. This parallel block is in series with resistor R3 = 1.25 ohms, across which an ideal voltmeter V is connected in parallel.

pilot_atoms.title: Resistance of wire recast to half its original radius

question.statement: A uniform wire of length $l$ and radius $r$ has a resistance of $100\,\Omega$. It is recast into a wire of radius $\frac{r}{2}$. The resistance of new wire will be ________ $\Omega$.

pilot_atoms.title: Ammeter and voltmeter readings in a DC circuit with parallel and series resistors

figure_refs.caption: Circuit diagram with $R_1 = 5\,\Omega$ and $R_2 = 15\,\Omega$ in parallel, each branch containing a resistor, with an ammeter (A) in series with $R_1$. This parallel combination is connected in series with $R_3 = 1.25\,\Omega$, across which a voltmeter (V) is connected. The circuit is powered by an EMF source $E = 20\text{ V}$.
figure_refs.alt_text: Electrical circuit diagram with a DC voltage source E = 20 V. Two resistors R1 = 5 ohms (with ammeter A in series) and R2 = 15 ohms are connected in parallel. This parallel block is connected in series with R3 = 1.25 ohms. A voltmeter V is connected in parallel across the R1-R2 parallel combination.

dag_edges.evidence: Physical quantities in 1D motion require dimensional consistency
dag_edges.rationale: Displacement, velocity, and acceleration are defined with specific dimensional units.

dag_edges.evidence: Projectile motion is two independent orthogonal 1D rectilinear motions
dag_edges.rationale: Galilean independence of x and y axes requires 1D kinematic equations.

dag_edges.evidence: Acceleration from kinematics is coupled to net force in Newton's second law
dag_edges.rationale: Kinematic acceleration is the dynamical effect caused by net external force.

dag_edges.evidence: 2D vector resolution required for resolving forces along perpendicular axes
dag_edges.rationale: Free body diagram force decomposition relies on 2D planar vector components.

dag_edges.evidence: Normal reaction force from Newton's laws determines maximum static friction
dag_edges.rationale: Frictional limits depend directly on normal contact force determined via FBD equilibrium.

dag_edges.evidence: Work-Energy theorem is derived from Newton's second law via line integration
dag_edges.rationale: Integrating F = m dv/dt with respect to spatial displacement yields the Work-Energy Theorem.

dag_edges.evidence: Dissipative non-conservative work requires friction concept
dag_edges.rationale: Energy conservation accounting requires identifying non-conservative friction work.

dag_edges.evidence: Center of mass dynamics follows Newton's second law for a system of particles
dag_edges.rationale: Internal forces cancel in pairs by Newton's third law, giving F_ext = M a_cm.

dag_edges.evidence: Collision mechanics requires simultaneous energy and momentum balance
dag_edges.rationale: Elastic and inelastic collisions partition kinetic energy in the CM frame.

dag_edges.evidence: Rotational kinematics maps circular arc length and tangential velocity to angle
dag_edges.rationale: Rigid body rotation extends circular motion kinematics to continuous mass distributions.

dag_edges.evidence: Parallel axis theorem requires moment of inertia about the center of mass
dag_edges.rationale: I = I_cm + M d^2 relies fundamentally on center of mass definition.

dag_edges.evidence: Rotational dynamics equation tau = I alpha requires moment of inertia
dag_edges.rationale: Moment of inertia I is the rotational inertia resisting angular acceleration.

dag_edges.evidence: Torque is the rotational analog of force tau = r x F
dag_edges.rationale: Newton's laws applied to individual particle elements yield torque balance.

dag_edges.evidence: Conservation of angular momentum requires tau_ext = dL/dt = 0
dag_edges.rationale: Zero net external torque is the governing condition for angular momentum conservation.

dag_edges.evidence: Angular momentum conservation is the rotational analog of linear momentum conservation
dag_edges.rationale: Rotational invariance of physical laws yields angular momentum conservation by Noether's theorem.

dag_edges.evidence: Hydrostatic pressure equilibrium is derived from static force balance
dag_edges.rationale: Pressure variation dP = -rho g dy balances the weight of a fluid element.

dag_edges.evidence: Archimedes principle is the surface pressure integral over a submerged body
dag_edges.rationale: Buoyant force is the net upward hydrostatic pressure force on the body surface.

dag_edges.evidence: Calorimetry and thermal expansion rely on fundamental thermal units
dag_edges.rationale: Heat capacity and temperature scales require clear dimensional framing.

dag_edges.evidence: Heat transfer Q in first law is quantified via calorimetry and heat capacities
dag_edges.rationale: First law dQ = dU + dW relates thermal heat transfer to mechanical work.

dag_edges.evidence: Thermodynamic boundary work dW = P dV is mechanical work on moving boundary
dag_edges.rationale: Boundary work connects thermal system expansion to mechanical force displacement.

dag_edges.evidence: Adiabatic process is the dQ = 0 condition of the first law of thermodynamics
dag_edges.rationale: dU = -dW leads to P V^gamma = constant for reversible adiabatic expansions.

dag_edges.evidence: Electrostatic force follows inverse square vector force law
dag_edges.rationale: Electrostatic equilibrium requires vector balance of Coulomb and mechanical forces.

dag_edges.evidence: Electric potential is conservative potential energy per unit charge
dag_edges.rationale: Conservative electrostatic field integral yields potential difference delta V.

dag_edges.evidence: Gauss's law is the flux formulation of Coulomb inverse square field
dag_edges.rationale: Flux of inverse square central field over closed surface gives enclosed charge / epsilon_0.

dag_edges.evidence: Internal electric field in conductor drives steady drift velocity
dag_edges.rationale: Electric force F = q E accelerates conduction electrons between lattice collisions.

dag_edges.evidence: Resistance R = rho L / A derives from microscopic current density J = sigma E
dag_edges.rationale: Macroscopic Ohm's law V = IR integrates microscopic field along wire geometry.

dag_edges.evidence: Kirchhoff's loop and junction laws require resistive potential drops and junctions
dag_edges.rationale: Circuit analysis models components with discrete resistances obeying V = IR.

dag_edges.evidence: Kirchhoff's Voltage Law is energy conservation around closed loop
dag_edges.rationale: Net work done in moving unit charge around closed electrostatic loop is zero.

dag_edges.evidence: Ray paths trace particle trajectories in optical media
dag_edges.rationale: Geometric optics rectilinear propagation models light as ray trajectories.

dag_edges.evidence: Total internal reflection occurs when angle of refraction exceeds 90 degrees
dag_edges.rationale: Setting r = 90 in Snell's law n1 sin(i) = n2 sin(r) yields critical angle sin(theta_c) = n2/n1.
